name: Michael Hedges
editorial_article: Michael Alden Hedges (1953–1997) was an American composer, guitarist, and multi-instrumentalist whose innovative, percussive approach to the steel-string acoustic guitar fundamentally reshaped the instrument's possibilities in the late 20th century. While frequently categorized under the Windham Hill label's new-age umbrella, Hedges viewed himself primarily as a composer, drawing profound creative inspiration from 20th-century classical icons like Igor Stravinsky, Edgard Varèse, and Steve Reich. His technique was a masterclass in complexity; he utilized unconventional alternate tunings, intricate string damping, two-handed tapping, and syncopated percussive slaps against the guitar's body, often blurring the lines between a single instrument and a full ensemble. His landmark 1984 album, *Aerial Boundaries*, remains a seminal release, capturing the technical brilliance and emotional depth that defined his career. Beyond his technical prowess, Hedges was a sensitive songwriter who sought to bridge the gap between his instrumental virtuosity and his vocal compositions. His life and career were tragically cut short in 1997 by a fatal car accident in Mendocino County, California, yet his influence remains pervasive among modern fingerstyle guitarists. He was posthumously honored with a Grammy Award for his final studio album, *Oracle*. Throughout his career, he maintained a deep, collaborative relationship with bassist Michael Manring, who provided the foundational support for most of his recorded output.
